approach: Add `check_root_cause_criterion(reading, request)` to crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, placed right after `check_code_survey`, with one `step!(check_root_cause_criterion(reading, request))` line in `refusing_check` after `step!(check_code_survey(reading))`. It applies only when the reading has a capability and no question, the class is `code` or `tests`, and the request has a whole-word wrong-output cue (fix, fixes, fixed, wrong, incorrect, stale, broken, bug, bugs, regression, failure, failures). Then it needs (a) a criterion of either kind that names the root cause (`root cause` or `root-cause`) and says where wrong items enter or why they are not excluded (a word starting enter, reach, exclu or filter), and (b) one Behavior criterion that names a test, real recorded or decided data (real, recorded, decided, stored, actual) and says it fails on the base. The error names each missing part in fixed phrases. A doc comment names the root cause and cites jobs 20261103-201526-t4qv and 20261103-231808-3gkq. Add unit tests in reading.rs, corpus cases in refusal_corpus.rs, one rule line and its test updates in briefs.rs, and one CHANGELOG entry. The check reads only the reading and the request text and costs no model call. Order after `check_code_survey` means a bug-fix corpus case needs a `Code survey:` assumption to reach the new check.

decisions.choice: Fix at the reading gate as a new `step!` in `refusing_check`, not in the reader prompt or in xtask/decisions.
decisions.reason: Both failed jobs were accepted because the gate did not require a diagnosis. The gate runs on every reading, first attempt or retry, with no model call. The corpus test `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` forces a refusing case. The reader prompt has 3 tokens of headroom (system facts, budget reader 1997 of 2000) and the brief puts it out of scope.

rejected.option: Add prose to the reader prompt
rejected.why: Out of scope; no headroom; prose is not enforced.
It is a single instance of the class; the brief drops it.

rejected.option: Run new tests on a scratch copy of the base in the pipeline
rejected.why: A pipeline change, left for a separate job. This job requires only that a criterion say the test fails on the base.

decisions.choice: The root-cause criterion must contain `root cause` or `root-cause` AND a word starting enter, reach, exclu or filter.
decisions.reason: Athena's own root-cause requests carry the bullet `The root cause is named in the change description and fixed where it originates`. A reader that copies that bullet would pass a check for the phrase alone, which is the failure of both jobs. The extra word forces the criterion to say where wrong items enter or why they are not excluded.

rejected.why: The copied request bullet satisfies it with no diagnosis.
Brittle; refuses readings that state the diagnosis in other words.

decisions.choice: Bug cues are the strong words only (fix, fixes, fixed, wrong, incorrect, stale, broken, bug, bugs, regression, failure, failures), matched as whole words with `has_phrase` on `normalised` request text. `shows` and `lists` are not cues.
decisions.reason: `shows` and `lists` appear in ordinary feature requests (`add a page that lists jobs`), which would be refused for lacking a diagnosis. The accepted reading says `such as`, which leaves the list open. Whole-word matching keeps `prefix`, `debug` and `fixture` from matching.

rejected.option: Include shows and lists as the reading's example list does
rejected.why: Refuses feature work; criterion 3 requires feature requests to be untouched.

decisions.choice: The test criterion must be one Behavior criterion that contains all three: a `test` word, a real-data word, and `fail` with the whole word `base`.
decisions.reason: Introspection 20261105-051344-q9fv records tests that pass on the base. Naming the base-failing run in the criterion is the reading-level part in scope. Requiring all three in one criterion stops a data word in one criterion and a test word in another from passing.

rejected.option: Check only for a test word and a data word
rejected.why: Does not require the test to fail on the base, which was the second repeated finding.

decisions.choice: Add the rule to `READING_RULES` in briefs.rs as a seventh line and update the briefs.rs tests.
decisions.reason: The reader should be told the rule before it is refused. READING_RULES is a section of the reader brief, not the always-loaded reader prompt set that has 3 tokens of headroom. briefs.rs is a listed deliverable.

rejected.option: Leave the reader unaware of the rule
rejected.why: The reader would be refused once and then re-read, so most bug-fix readings would pay a second read.

steps: Read crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs `check_code_survey` (3453), `has_phrase` (3293) and `normalised` (3833) once more, then write `check_root_cause_criterion(reading: &Reading, request: &str) -> Result<()>` after `check_code_survey`, with a doc comment in the style of its neighbours. The doc names the root cause (bug-fix readings were accepted with no diagnosis and no base-failing real-data test), cites jobs 20261103-201526-t4qv and 20261103-231808-3gkq, and has one paragraph with the exact sentence `This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended.`. Logic: return Ok when capability is None, question is Some, the class is not `code` or `tests`, or `normalised(request)` has none of the cue words as whole words (`has_phrase`). Otherwise find a criterion whose normalised text (with `-` read as a space) has the phrase `root cause` and a word starting enter, reach, exclu or filter. Also find one Behavior criterion with a `test` word, a real-data word (real, recorded, decided, stored, actual) and both `fail` and the whole word `base`. Bail with the fixed phrases `a criterion that names the root cause (where wrong items enter and why they are not excluded)` and `a criterion for a test built from real decided data that fails on the base`, each only when its part is missing. Begin the message `the reading was refused because ...` and say what to write.

Add `step!(check_root_cause_criterion(reading, request));` in `refusing_check`, right after `step!(check_code_survey(reading));`. Update the `check_reading_acceptance` doc line (3085-3090) to mention the new check. Do not call it directly from `check_reading_acceptance`.

risks.risk: A replay of past accepted readings may newly refuse more than 10 percent, because every Athena root-cause request begins `Fix the root cause` and so triggers the check. The brief's criteria declare no `expected N% of newly refused readings`; the 12 percent figure is only in the accepted reading's assumptions. The job could be held.
risks.mitigation: The check applies only to class code or tests with a capability and no question. The doc comment carries the sentence `This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended.` The CHANGELOG entry names the expected share. The producer reports that the criteria carry no declared share, so the verifier can judge it.

risks.risk: False refusals on feature requests that contain `failure` or `fix` for another reason, for example `retry on failure`.
risks.mitigation: The error says exactly what to write, and the reader is re-read once with the refusal as a correction. `shows` and `lists` are excluded as cues. Whole-word matching is covered by the `fixture`/`prefix` case.

risks.risk: The stricter root-cause wording rule (the criterion must also contain enter, reach, exclu or filter) is stricter than the accepted reading's `containing 'root cause'`. A reader may need a second read.
risks.mitigation: The rule line in READING_RULES and the error text give the exact wording. The reason for the extra word is in the decision record and the doc comment: the request's own bullet contains `root cause`.

risks.risk: Adding a line to the reader rules grows the brief past the `section.len() < 2400` assertion or the 220-byte line limit in briefs.rs.
risks.mitigation: Keep the line to 215 bytes or less, measure the section, and raise the limit in the test only by the measured need. Run `cargo test -p athena-context`.

risks.risk: A decline or question corpus case may trip another check first (for example a boundary scan of deliverables).
risks.mitigation: Build each case from `base_reading` and change one field, as the corpus header says. Copy the shape of the `declined` and `asking` readings in reading.rs (lines 7010-7015) and run the corpus test.

risks.risk: The corpus refuse case needs an `xtask/src/decisions.rs` deliverable that is not in `repo_files()`, so `check_boundary_and_repo_files` would refuse first.
risks.mitigation: Insert that path into the case's own `repo_files` set, not the shared function, so other cases are unchanged.

demonstrations.method: A unit test in reading.rs tests (`root_cause_check_is_a_step_and_documents_its_cause`) reads its own source with `include_str!("reading.rs")`. It asserts that the body of `refusing_check` contains `step!(check_root_cause_criterion(reading, request))` after the `check_code_survey` step. It asserts that the doc paragraph before `pub fn check_root_cause_criterion` contains `20261103-201526-t4qv`, `20261103-231808-3gkq`, `no diagnosis`, `base-failing real-data test` and `This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended.`
demonstrations.observes: The test passes: the function exists, the step line exists in order, and the doc comment names the cause and both jobs.

demonstrations.method: The corpus drives `athena_core::reading::refusing_check` through `run(c)` and `corpus_cases_get_the_expected_outcome`. Case `bug-fix-reading-without-root-cause` is rebuilt from the shape of job 20261103-201526-t4qv: a request `Fix the root cause ... decisions page lists rejected proposals` with dash bullets. The reading has class `code`, a `Code survey:` assumption naming `crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs` and a Behavior criterion with no root-cause criterion. A local `repo_files` insert adds the `xtask/src/decisions.rs` deliverable. It expects `Refuse("check_root_cause_criterion")`. Case `bug-fix-reading-with-root-cause-and-real-data-test` is the same reading plus a root-cause criterion (`The root cause is that approved and rejected proposals both enter the page because the filter does not exclude rejected ones`) and a Behavior criterion (`Run cargo test: a test built from real approved and rejected decisions fails on the base tree and passes with the change`). It expects Accept. Case `root-cause-request-bullet-copied-is-not-a-diagnosis` copies the request bullet `The root cause is named in the change description and fixed where it originates` and expects the same refusal. Case `bug-fix-reading-without-base-failing-real-data-test` has a root-cause criterion but a Behavior criterion that says only `the new test passes`, and expects the same refusal.
demonstrations.observes: `corpus_cases_get_the_expected_outcome` passes: the three refuse cases are refused by `check_root_cause_criterion` (the first to refuse) and the accept case is accepted. `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` passes with the new step.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the check, the three refuse cases are accepted. `corpus_cases_get_the_expected_outcome` then reports `expected Refuse("check_root_cause_criterion"), got accepted`, and `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` reports no case for it.

The fixture is a `Case` built by the existing `case(..)` helper from `base_reading` (refusal_corpus.rs:106,175). The test changes the class, assumptions, criteria and `repo_files` on the case. The seam exists. Plan step 4 adds the cases and the `bug-fix-root-cause` entry in `INPUT_FORMS` (array length 17 to 18).

demonstrations.method: Corpus accept cases for non-bug work: `feature-request-code-reading-is-not-a-bug-fix` (code, survey, Behavior criterion, request `Add a --json flag to athena status`, no cue); `cue-inside-a-longer-word-is-not-a-cue` (code reading, request `Add a test fixture for the prefix parser`); `bug-fix-docs-reading-is-exempt` (the docs base reading with request `Fix the typo in the guide`); `bug-fix-decline-is-exempt` (capability None with a decline reason); `bug-fix-reading-with-a-question-is-exempt` (question set). The same test asserts that the unit-test fixture `code_reading` with request `change the reading rules` stays accepted by `accept`.

demonstrations.method: Unit test `root_cause_refusal_names_what_is_missing` in reading.rs. It builds a bug-fix `code_reading` with the `SURVEY` assumption and one Behavior criterion that has neither a root cause nor a base-failing real-data test. It calls `check_root_cause_criterion(&reading, "Fix the wrong output of the page")`. It asserts the error contains `a criterion that names the root cause (where wrong items enter and why they are not excluded)` and `a criterion for a test built from real decided data that fails on the base`. Further assertions: with the root-cause criterion present, only the second phrase appears; with only the real-data test criterion present, only the first appears. The second assertion covers the case where the test criterion is Content and not Behavior.
demonstrations.observes: Both phrases are in the error when both parts are missing, and only the missing part's phrase appears otherwise.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the check the call returns Ok and `unwrap_err` panics. A message that names only one part fails the two-phrase assertion.
